docs.text: Welcome to the Gared Graphics WordPress documentation ¶ This documentation shows you how to update your website yourself: the text and photos on each page, your contact details, menus, portfolio projects, blog posts and the forms on the Contact page. Your site runs on WordPress , with a custom theme built by Coalition Technologies to match your design. Most of what you see can be changed from the WordPress dashboard without touching any code. Logging in ¶ Go to /wp-admin/ on your website (add it to the end of your website address). Enter the username and password you were given, then click Log In . You'll land on the Dashboard . The menu on the left takes you everywhere you need to go. Tip While you're logged in and viewing your site, a dark bar at the top of every page gives you shortcuts such as Edit Page and Customize . Where things are ¶ In the left menu What you change there Pages The content of Home, About Us, Services, Portfolio, Contact Us and the other pages (see Editing pages ) Posts Your blog articles and their categories (see Blog posts ) Portfolio Your portfolio projects and their categories (see Portfolio projects ) Media Every image and file you've uploaded (see Images ) Forms Messages and quote requests sent through the website's forms (see Forms ) Appearance → Customize Logo, contact details, header, footer, social links and other site-wide settings (see Site settings ) Appearance → Menus The links in the header and footer menus Please don't change ¶ Some areas control how the site is built rather than what it says. Changing them can break the layout, so please leave them as they are, or ask us first: ACF (field groups): these define the editing fields for each section of your pages. Appearance → Themes : switching theme would replace your site's design. Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS : code that changes the site's styling. Plugins : they power the forms, the editing fields and backups. Pages → Sample Page : a reference page that shows how every kind of content looks on your site (headings, text, links, lists, buttons, quotes, tables and more), including how buttons and links change when you point at them. It's hidden from search engines, the menus and the site search, so visitors won't come across it. Open it whenever you want to see how something will look before adding it to a page. In this documentation ¶ Editing pages : how the page editor works, the page header, and the kinds of fields. What's on each page: Home , About Us , Services , Portfolio , Contact Us . Portfolio projects : adding projects and their categories. Blog posts : writing posts, categories and comments. Forms : reading messages and quote requests, and who gets the emails. Images : sizes, file names and alt text. Site settings : logo, contact details, header and footer, social links, menus. For developers Custom WordPress theme ( Gared Graphics ) with page sections built as ACF Pro blocks; field definitions are saved as JSON in the theme ( acf-json/ ), so change them in code, not under ACF in the dashboard. Forms use Gravity Forms. Theme code is managed in its own git repository.

docs.text: Blog posts ¶ Your articles appear on the Blog page (newest first), in the Blog section of the home page, in their category pages and in the sitemap. Writing a post ¶ Go to Posts → Add New . The editor works like the portfolio editor (see Portfolio projects ): Title : the post's headline. Content : type your article. Click + to add headings, images, lists or quotes between paragraphs. Use Heading blocks to break up long posts; they make articles easier to read and help search engines. Featured image : in the right-hand panel. It's shown on the post's card and at the top of the post. Landscape, at least 1200px wide. Excerpt : the short summary shown on the post's card (about 20 words). Without one, the card uses the first words of the post. Categories : in the right-hand panel, under Categories . Create new ones there or under Posts → Categories . Publish : makes the post live. To publish later, click the date next to Publish and pick a future date first. How many posts per page ¶ The Blog page shows 9 posts at a time, with page numbers below. Change it under Settings → Reading → Blog pages show at most . Keep it to a multiple of 3 (6, 9, 12) so the last row of the grid is always full. Comments ¶ Visitors can comment on posts. A person's first comment waits for your approval; after that, their comments appear straight away. Approve, reply to or delete comments under Comments in the left menu. Mark unwanted comments as Spam rather than deleting them; it helps WordPress recognise spam.

docs.text: Editing pages ¶ Every page is made of sections , stacked from top to bottom: a photo banner, a block of text beside an image, a row of cards and so on. Each section has its own fields for the text, images and buttons, so you change the words and pictures while the design stays consistent. Opening a page ¶ Go to Pages in the left menu. Find the page, for example About Us . Hover over it and click Edit . Or, while viewing the page on your site, click Edit Page in the dark bar at the top. The editor ¶ The page itself : a live preview of each section. Click a section to select it. Section toolbar : appears above the selected section. Use the arrows to move it up or down, the dotted handle to drag it, and ⋮ for more options such as Duplicate or Delete . Block tab : shows the selected section's fields. (The Page tab next to it holds the page's own settings; see below.) Fields : change the text, images and buttons here. The preview updates as you type. Save : publishes your changes. Nothing changes on the live site until you click it. Add a section (+): opens the list of sections. Ours are under CT Theme ; type a name such as Text and Image to find one quickly. List view : an outline of every section on the page, handy for jumping to one or dragging sections into a new order. Bigger editing area Click Open Expanded Editor at the top of a section's fields to edit them in a larger window. The page header ¶ Most pages start with a header: a wide photo with a dark box holding the page title. Its settings are in the Page tab of the right-hand panel. Page tab: the page's own settings. Featured image : the photo behind the header. Click it to replace it. Without one, the page uses the default photo set in Site settings . Scroll down the Page tab to the Page header fields: Heading : the large title in the header. Leave it empty to use the page's name. Description : an optional line of text under the title. If you type the site's phone number exactly as it appears in Site settings, it automatically becomes a tap-to-call link. The home page has no page header; it starts with the large photo banner (the Hero section). Kinds of fields ¶ Every section uses the same few kinds of fields. Under each field there's a short grey note saying what it's for (for example Landscape photo, at least 900px wide ). Field How to use it Text A single line, such as a heading or the small label above it (we call that label the eyebrow ). Text area Paragraphs. Leave a blank line between paragraphs. Icon Pick an icon from the list. Icons come with the theme. Switch ( Show phone number , Show steps …) Turns part of a section on or off. Images, buttons and lists of cards work a little differently, so they're shown below. Images ¶ Edit (pencil, appears when you hover over the photo): change the photo's details, such as its alt text. Remove (✕): takes the photo out. An Add Image button then appears in its place. Click Add Image (or the empty image area) to open the image picker: Upload files : drag a photo in from your computer, or click Select Files . Media Library : every image already on the site. Search media : find an image by name. Click an image to select it (a blue tick appears). Alt Text : a short description of the photo for screen readers and search engines (see Images ). Select : puts the chosen image into the field. Buttons and links ¶ Edit (pencil): change where the button goes or what it says. Remove (✕): hides the button. Click Select Link to add it back. URL : the address the button opens. For a page on your site, use Search (4) instead of typing it. Link Text : the words on the button. Open link in a new tab : only for other websites; leave it unticked for your own pages. Search : type part of a page's name and click it in the list; the URL fills in for you. Update : saves the link. ( Cancel leaves it as it was.) Lists of cards, steps and points ¶ Cards, steps, milestones, checklist points and similar lists are made of rows : one row per card. Lists are easier to edit in the bigger window: click Open Expanded Editor at the top of the section's fields. Row number : drag it up or down to change the order. + (appears when you hover over a row): adds a new row just above this one. − : removes this row. Add button under the list (named after what it adds, for example Add milestone ): adds a row at the end. The design is laid out for a certain number of rows; the grey note under the list says how many fit best (for example Three cards make one row on desktop ). Worked example: change the photo and heading in "Our story" ¶ This walks through a typical edit on the About Us page from start to finish. Open the page. Go to Pages , hover over About Us and click Edit (see Opening a page ). Select the section. Click anywhere on the Our story section in the editor. Its toolbar appears above it, and the Block tab on the right shows About: Story with its fields (see The editor ). Change the heading. Click in the Heading field and type the new heading. The preview updates as you type. Replace the photo. Scroll down the fields to Image , hover over the photo and click ✕ to remove it, then click Add Image . In Media Library pick the new photo (or Upload files to add one from your computer), check its Alt Text , and click Select (see Images ). Save. Click Save at the top right. A message confirms it's saved. Check it. Click the View page icon (the square with an arrow, left of the panel buttons) to see the live page. Tip Changed your mind before saving? Use Undo at the top left, or leave the page without saving. After saving, use Revisions (see Undoing mistakes ). Adding, moving and removing sections ¶ Add : click + (6 above), find the section under CT Theme , and click it. It's added below the selected section with sample text; replace it with yours. Move : select the section and use the arrows in its toolbar, or drag it in List view . Remove : select it, click ⋮ in its toolbar, then Delete . Sections are designed for the page they're named after ( About: Story for About Us, Services: Process for Services), but the general ones ( Text and Image , Feature Cards , Image Cards , Contact Band ) can be used on any page. Undoing mistakes ¶ Before you save: use Undo (the curved arrow at the top) or leave the page without saving. After you save: open the Page tab, click Revisions , pick an earlier version and click Restore This Revision . What's on each page ¶ Home About Us Services Portfolio Contact Us The Blog page lists your posts automatically (see Blog posts ), and the Sitemap page lists every page, project and post on its own. Terms of Use is plain text you can edit like a document.

docs.text: Forms ¶ The site has two forms, both on the Contact Us page: Contact Us (general messages) and Request a Quote . They're run by Gravity Forms , under Forms in the left menu. Forms in the left menu. Contact Us : the message form. Request a Quote : the quote form. Entries : how many messages each form has received. Click the number to read them. Reading messages ¶ Every message sent through a form is saved as an entry , even if an email goes astray. Go to Forms → Entries (or click a form's entry count). Pick the form from the menu at the top if needed. Click an entry to read it. Unread entries are shown in bold; use the star to flag ones to follow up. To keep a copy outside the website, go to Forms → Import/Export → Export Entries , choose the form and the fields, and download a spreadsheet (CSV). Who gets the emails ¶ When someone sends a form, two emails go out: To your team : the full message, with the sender's email set as the reply address, so you can simply click Reply . To the visitor : a confirmation that their message or quote request arrived, with a copy of what they sent. These are set under Forms , then hover over a form and click Notifications . Please ask us before changing notifications Notifications control where messages are delivered. A wrong address means quote requests go missing, so let us know if your team's address changes and we'll update it and send a test. The thank-you message ¶ After sending, the visitor sees a short thank-you message in place of the form. To change its wording: Forms , hover over the form, Settings → Confirmations . Spam protection ¶ Both forms are protected against spam robots by an invisible check from Google (reCAPTCHA) and a hidden trap field. Real visitors don't see either. You may notice a small reCAPTCHA badge in the bottom-right corner of the Contact page; it needs to stay there. Fields and wording ¶ To change a form's questions (labels, the packaging types, quantity ranges), go to Forms , hover over the form and click Edit . Because the quote buttons on the Services page pre-select a packaging type, please ask us before renaming or removing Sleeves , Boxes or Trays .

docs.text: Images ¶ Good photos make the site. A few simple habits keep them sharp and quick to load. Before you upload ¶ Photos as JPG , logos and graphics with transparency as PNG. Size : each image field says how wide the photo should be (for example at least 1200px wide ). About twice the width it appears on screen keeps it sharp on high-resolution screens. There's no need to go much bigger: very large files (4000px straight from a camera) only slow the site down. Around 2400px wide is plenty for the widest photos. Shape : most photos are shown in a fixed shape (often 4:3) and cropped to fit. Keep the important part of the picture near the middle. File name : describe the photo, with hyphens instead of spaces, for example gared-graphics-food-trays.jpg . It helps search engines. Uploading ¶ Click Add Image (or Set featured image ) in any image field and choose Upload files , or upload several at once under Media → Add New . WordPress automatically makes smaller copies for phones and tablets, so you only upload one version. Alt text ¶ In the Media Library, each image has an Alternative Text box. Describe what the photo shows in a short sentence, for example Printed food trays stacked on a production line . Screen readers read it to visitors who can't see the image, and search engines use it too. Leave it empty only for purely decorative images. Replacing a photo ¶ Pick a new image in the field that shows it (a section, the featured image, or Site settings), then Save . The old image stays in the Media Library; delete it there if it's no longer used anywhere.

docs.text: Portfolio projects ¶ Each project you've produced is a Portfolio item . Projects appear automatically in the gallery on the Portfolio page, in the Portfolio section of the home page (newest first), and in the sitemap. Each one also gets its own page. Adding or editing a project ¶ Go to Portfolio → Add New (or Portfolio , then click a project's name to edit it). Title : the project's name, shown on its card and as the heading of its page. Description : the text on the project's page. Type straight into the page; press Enter for a new paragraph. Featured image : the photo on the project's card and at the top of its page. Click it to set or replace it. Use a landscape photo at least 1200px wide; cards show it at 4:3. Excerpt : a one-line summary used where a short description is needed, for example in search results. Save (or Publish for a new project): makes your changes live. Categories ¶ Scroll down the right-hand panel to Categories . Categories : tick the category the project belongs to. The first one ticked is shown on the project's card, and it decides which filter button finds the project in the gallery. One category per project works best. Add Category : creates a new category. Manage all of them under Portfolio → Categories (rename, or change the web address part called the slug ). Note New categories appear in the gallery's filter automatically, behind the + more button. To make one of the three main buttons, change Main categories in the gallery section on the Portfolio page (see Portfolio ). Removing a project ¶ In Portfolio , hover over the project and click Trash . It disappears from the site straight away and stays in Trash for 30 days, where you can restore it.

The first one ticked is shown on the project's card, and it decides which filter button finds the project in the gallery. One category per project works best. Add Category : creates a new category. Manage all of them under Portfolio → Categories (rename, or change the web address part called the slug ). Note New categories appear in the gallery's filter automatically, behind the + more button. To make one of the three main buttons, change Main categories in the gallery section on the Portfolio page (see Portfolio ).

docs.text: In Portfolio , hover over the project and click Trash . It disappears from the site straight away and stays in Trash for 30 days, where you can restore it.

docs.text: Site settings ¶ Your logo, contact details, header, footer and social links are set once and used across the whole site. You change them in the Customizer , which shows a live preview of the site as you type. Opening the Customizer ¶ Go to Appearance → Customize in the left menu (or click Customize in the dark bar at the top of the site while you're logged in). Header : logo, phone number and the button at the top right. Contact details : phone, email, address and opening hours. Page header : the default photo at the top of pages. Call to action : the burgundy band at the end of blog posts and projects. Footer : footer logo, headings, copyright line and social links. Menus : the links in the header and footer. Publish : nothing changes on the live site until you click it. Preview first, then publish Every change shows straight away in the preview on the right, but visitors don't see it yet. When you're happy, click Publish at the top. If you change your mind, close the Customizer with the ✕ at the top left and leave without publishing. Header ¶ Logo : click Change image to pick a new logo from the Media Library or upload one. Use a PNG with a transparent background , at least 440 pixels wide , so it stays sharp on high-resolution screens. The same logo is used in the footer and in the emails the forms send, unless you set a separate footer logo. Logo width on desktop : how wide the logo appears on large screens, between 120 and 220 pixels (180 is the design's size). On phones and tablets it's shown smaller automatically. Show phone number : shows or hides the phone number next to the menu. Header button label : the text on the burgundy button at the top right (currently Request a Quote ). Header button URL : where the button goes. /contact-us/#quote opens the quote form on the Contact page; leave it empty to link to the Contact Us page. Contact details ¶ These are used everywhere they appear on the site: the header, the footer, the Contact page and the contact sections on other pages. Change them here once and they update everywhere. Phone (as displayed) : the number exactly as visitors should see it, e.g. (805) 987-8577 . It's also made into a tap-to-call link. Phone link override : leave empty. Only needed if the number people should dial differs from the one shown (for example with an extension), written as tel:+18059878577 . Email : the email address shown on the site. This doesn't change where form messages are delivered. Facility address : one line per row. It's shown on the Contact page and used for the map and the Get directions link. Business hours : one line per row, shown on the Contact page. Page header ¶ Default image : the photo shown at the top of pages that don't have their own Featured Image . To give a single page its own photo, set the Featured Image when editing that page. Leave the default empty for a plain dark band. Call to action ¶ The burgundy band shown at the end of blog posts, portfolio projects and the "page not found" page: Heading : the band's headline. Button label and Button URL : the button's text and link (leave the URL empty to link to the Contact Us page). Footer ¶ Footer logo : leave empty to use the header logo, or choose a different version for the dark footer. Footer logo width : between 100 and 240 pixels (160 is the design's size). Menu heading : the title above the footer menu (currently Explore ). Contact heading : the title above the footer's contact details (currently Contact ). Show phone number and Show email : show or hide them in the footer. Copyright line : leave empty for "© {year} Gared Graphics. All rights reserved."; the year updates itself. Social links ¶ Scroll down in the Footer section for the social media addresses. Facebook URL Instagram URL X (Twitter) URL Pinterest URL LinkedIn URL Paste the full address of your profile page, e.g. https://www.facebook.com/yourpage . Each one shows as an icon in the contact panel on the Contact page; leave a field empty to hide that icon. Menus ¶ Appearance → Menus (or Menus in the Customizer) controls three menus: Menu Where it appears Primary The main menu in the header Footer The links in the footer Legal The small links next to the copyright line (Sitemap, Terms of Use) To add a page, tick it in the list on the left, click Add to Menu , drag it into place, then click Save Menu . Drag items to change their order; click an item's arrow and Remove to take it off the menu. Site Identity ¶ Site Identity in the Customizer holds the Site Title (used in browser tabs, search results and the copyright line), the Tagline , and the Site Icon : the small image shown in browser tabs. Use a square image at least 512 × 512 pixels.

docs.text: Contact Us ¶ Open it from Pages → Contact Us → Edit . The page header (title, description and photo) is set in the Page tab; see The page header . The phone number in the description becomes a call link automatically. How to edit a section Open the page in the editor, click the section you want to change, and its fields appear in the Block tab on the right. Change them, then click Save . New to the editor? See Editing pages , including a worked example . The page has two form sections (a message form and a quote form) and a map. The forms' fields and emails are managed under Forms ; see Forms . Send us a message ¶ Section: Form Section . Click it in the editor to see these fields in the Block tab. Field What it changes Form Which form to show (here Contact Us ). Heading, Intro The text above the form. Contact heading The small heading in the dark panel ( Contact details ). Show phone number, Show email Show or hide them in the panel. Show facility address Shows the address with a Get directions link. Show business hours Shows the opening hours. Show social links Shows the social media icons. Only profiles with an address in Site settings appear. Show steps Shows the numbered What happens next list instead (used by the quote form). Background Light grey or white. Use white for a form section right after a grey one, so the two read as separate sections. The phone, email, address and hours all come from Site settings . Request a quote ¶ Section: Form Section , with the Request a Quote form and Show steps on. Click it in the editor to see these fields in the Block tab. Field What it changes Steps heading The heading above the steps ( What happens next ). Steps One row per step: Title and Text , numbered automatically. The header's Request a Quote button and the Services page buttons link straight to this form. Find our facility ¶ Section: Location Map . Click it in the editor to see these fields in the Block tab. Field What it changes Eyebrow, Heading, Text The label, heading and optional text. The map, the address beside it and the Get directions button all use the Facility address in Site settings . Change the address there and the map moves with it.
